courses.course_name: Bachelor of Science in Management Accounting
courses.course_description:
The Bachelor of Science in Management Accounting (BSMA) is a degree program focused on the use of accounting and financial information to support internal business management and decision-making. Students learn how to prepare, analyze, and interpret financial and operational information that can help organizations plan, control operations, manage costs, evaluate performance, and make informed business decisions.
The program covers management accounting, financial accounting, cost accounting, budgeting, financial analysis, taxation, auditing, accounting information systems, and other business-related areas. Unlike programs focused primarily on external financial reporting and public accountancy, management accounting emphasizes the use of accounting information for planning, internal decision-making, performance evaluation, and organizational management .
career_paths: Other accounting, finance, and business-related positions

It also covers the efficient utilization, conservation, and management of natural and renewable resources to enhance human health in harmony with the environment .

The program integrates environmental science, urban and regional planning, land use planning, geography, economics, public policy, and social sciences to address issues involving land development, infrastructure, environmental protection, disaster risk reduction, and community resilience. Students develop competencies in comprehensive land use planning, environmental assessment, spatial analysis, policy formulation, geographic information systems (GIS), development planning, and stakeholder engagement to formulate sustainable and evidence-based planning solutions for government, private organizations, and communities.
obtainable_skills: Disaster risk reduction and climate resilience planning
career_paths: Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Planner

courses.course_name: Bachelor of Science in Environmental Science
courses.course_description: The Bachelor of Science in Environmental Science (BS ES) is a four-year interdisciplinary undergraduate program that prepares students to understand environmental systems and address environmental problems through scientific investigation and sustainable resource management. The program integrates biological sciences, chemistry, physics, earth sciences, social sciences, and environmental policy to examine the interactions between human activities and the natural environment. Students develop competencies in environmental assessment, ecosystem management, pollution prevention and control, environmental monitoring, conservation, environmental planning, scientific research, and sustainable development. Graduates are equipped to develop science-based solutions for environmental protection, resource conservation, and environmental management in government, industry, research institutions, and non-government organizations.

courses.course_name: Bachelor of Science in Family Economics major in Foods and Food Management
courses.course_description: The Bachelor of Science in Family Economics major in Foods and Food Management is a four-year undergraduate program that prepares students to apply principles of food science, nutrition, family resource management, and food service administration in promoting the health and well-being of individuals, families, and communities. The program combines scientific knowledge with management principles to prepare graduates for careers involving food production, nutrition, institutional food service, and consumer welfare. Students develop competencies in food preparation, food safety, nutrition planning, menu development, food service operations, family resource management, consumer education, and research while emphasizing efficient management of food-related resources and services.

courses.course_name: Bachelor of Science in Agricultural Economics major in Farm Management and Production Economics
courses.course_description: The Bachelor of Science in Agricultural Economics major in Farm Management and Production Economics is a four-year undergraduate program that prepares students to apply economic principles, business management, and quantitative analysis to agricultural production and farm enterprises. The program integrates agricultural sciences with economics to improve farm profitability, production efficiency, resource allocation, agribusiness decision-making, and sustainable agricultural development. Students develop competencies in farm planning, production economics, financial analysis, enterprise management, agricultural policy analysis, marketing, and economic research to support agricultural producers, agribusiness firms, cooperatives, government agencies, and rural development organizations.

courses.course_name: Bachelor of Arts major in Fashion Design and Merchandising
courses.course_description: The Bachelor of Arts major in Fashion Design and Merchandising is a four-year undergraduate program that prepares students to create, develop, produce, market, and manage fashion products and brands. The program combines artistic creativity, design principles, garment construction, textile knowledge, merchandising, branding, marketing, and entrepreneurship to prepare graduates for careers in the fashion and apparel industry. Students develop competencies in fashion illustration, apparel design, textile selection, pattern making, garment production, fashion merchandising, visual presentation, branding, trend forecasting, and sustainable fashion practices while integrating design innovation with business and consumer needs.

courses.course_name: Bachelor of Fine Arts
courses.course_description: The Bachelor of Fine Arts (BFA) is a four-year undergraduate program that prepares students for professional practice in the visual arts and creative industries. The program develops artistic creativity, technical competence, critical thinking, aesthetic sensitivity, and professional ethics through studio-based learning, research, and creative production. Students gain competencies in drawing, painting, sculpture, printmaking, photography, digital media, visual communication, design theory, art history, and professional practice while producing original works that contribute to cultural development and creative industries.

courses.course_name: Bachelor of Science in Fisheries
courses.course_description: The Bachelor of Science in Fisheries (BSF) is a four-year undergraduate program that prepares students to sustainably manage, develop, conserve, and utilize fisheries and aquatic resources. The program integrates biological sciences, aquatic ecology, aquaculture, capture fisheries, post-harvest technology, fisheries economics, resource management, and fisheries laws to produce competent fisheries professionals capable of supporting food security, environmental sustainability, and the fisheries industry. Students acquire scientific, technical, and managerial competencies needed for fisheries production, aquatic resource conservation, fisheries research, extension services, entrepreneurship, and policy implementation while addressing national and regional fisheries development needs.
obtainable_skills: Fish health and aquatic animal disease management

courses.course_name: Bachelor of Science in Food Technology
courses.course_description: The Bachelor of Science in Food Technology (BSFT) is a four-year undergraduate program that prepares students to apply scientific and technological principles to the processing, preservation, packaging, quality assurance, safety, and development of food products. The program integrates food science, chemistry, microbiology, engineering principles, nutrition, and quality management to produce competent food technologists capable of developing safe, nutritious, high-quality, and innovative food products for the food industry. Students develop competencies in food manufacturing, product research and development, food safety systems, laboratory analysis, quality assurance, and industrial food production while addressing national and global food security needs.

courses.course_name: Bachelor of Science in Forensic Science
courses.course_description: The Bachelor of Science in Forensic Science (BFSci) is a four-year undergraduate program under the Criminal Justice Education cluster that prepares students to apply scientific principles and laboratory techniques to criminal investigations and legal proceedings. The program combines natural sciences, criminal justice, forensic laboratory practice, crime scene investigation, evidence collection and analysis, forensic pathology, toxicology, DNA analysis, and legal procedures. Students receive extensive laboratory and field training to develop competencies in recognizing, collecting, preserving, examining, and interpreting physical evidence for use in criminal investigations and judicial processes.

courses.course_name: Bachelor of Science in Forestry
courses.course_description: The Bachelor of Science in Forestry (BS Forestry) is an undergraduate program focused on the scientific management, conservation, development, and sustainable use of forest resources and forest ecosystems. It prepares students to understand forest ecology and biodiversity while developing technical competencies for managing forests, watersheds, wildlife habitats, and forest-based resources. The program combines natural sciences with applied forestry, including forest resource assessment, forest management, silviculture, forest protection, biodiversity conservation, watershed management, forest products, and related environmental and resource-management practices.

courses.course_name: Bachelor of Science in Geology
courses.course_description: The Bachelor of Science in Geology (BS Geology) is a four-year undergraduate science program that focuses on the study of the Earth, its materials, structure, history, processes, and natural resources. Students examine minerals, rocks, fossils, geological formations, and the physical and chemical processes that shape the Earth's surface and interior. The program develops the scientific and field-based competencies needed to investigate geological conditions, conduct geological mapping and field studies, evaluate mineral and other earth resources, assess geological hazards, and interpret geological data.

courses.course_name: Bachelor of Arts in History
courses.course_description: The Bachelor of Arts in History (BA History) is a four-year humanities program that develops students' systematic understanding of the human past through the study, interpretation, analysis, and evaluation of historical events, societies, cultures, institutions, and historical evidence. The program trains students to critically examine primary and secondary sources, reconstruct and interpret historical developments, conduct historical research, and communicate evidence-based interpretations of the past. It also develops an understanding of Philippine, Asian, and world history and the relationships between historical events and broader social, political, economic, and cultural developments. History is therefore not limited to memorizing dates and events. The discipline involves research, source criticism, contextual analysis, interpretation, argumentation, and historical writing, enabling graduates to apply historical thinking in education, research, government, cultural institutions, media, heritage, and other fields.
career_paths: Teacher/History Educator subject to applicable teaching qualification and licensure requirements

courses.course_name: Bachelor of Science in Hospitality Management
courses.course_description: The Bachelor of Science in Hospitality Management (BSHM) is a four-year undergraduate program that prepares students for professional and managerial careers in the hospitality industry. It combines management principles with practical training in accommodation, food and beverage, guest services, hospitality operations, and related service industries. The program develops students' ability to manage hospitality establishments and service operations while applying principles of customer service, business management, human resources, marketing, financial management, risk management, and information technology. Students also receive practical preparation in areas such as food production and service, front-office operations, housekeeping, accommodation management, and other hospitality functions.

courses.course_name: Bachelor in Human Services
courses.course_description: The Bachelor in Human Services (BHumServ) is an undergraduate program that prepares students for professional work involving the delivery of human services to individuals, groups, organizations, and communities. The program develops an understanding of human development, human functioning, human-services systems, and the conditions affecting individuals and communities. Students are trained in helping skills, client support, intervention planning, program development and evaluation, research, communication, and ethical professional practice. The program also emphasizes practical field experience, allowing students to apply human-services knowledge and skills in actual educational, community, organizational, and other service environments.

courses.course_name: Bachelor of Science in Industrial Design
courses.course_description: The Bachelor of Science in Industrial Design (BSID) is an undergraduate design program that prepares students to conceptualize, develop, and evaluate products and designed objects that respond to functional, aesthetic, technological, cultural, environmental, and user requirements. The program combines creative design thinking with technical knowledge, materials and production considerations, visual communication, research, and design development. Students learn to transform ideas and identified user needs into product concepts and design solutions through processes such as research, ideation, visualization, prototyping, testing, refinement, and presentation. Industrial Design focuses on the development of products for human use and considers the relationship between the user, product, technology, materials, manufacturing processes, and environment.

courses.course_name: Bachelor of Industrial Engineering major in Industrial Engineering

It combines engineering, mathematics, statistics, operations research, management, economics, and human-factors principles.

courses.course_description: Interior Design is the art and science of planning, specifying, selecting, and organizing interior spaces, including surface finishes, materials, furniture, furnishings, fixtures, and other interior elements. The discipline focuses on creating interior environments that appropriately respond to their intended function, movement, character, users, and surrounding built environment. The program develops students' ability to identify and solve interior design problems, formulate design concepts and strategies, integrate design theories and philosophies, and communicate design proposals through visual, oral, written, and digital/virtual methods. It also incorporates knowledge of art and design history, period styles, materials, furniture, building construction, utilities, color, legislation, technology, and professional practice.

courses.course_name: Bachelor of Science in Internal Auditing
courses.course_description: The Bachelor of Science in Internal Auditing (BSIA) is an accounting and business program designed to prepare students for professional work in internal auditing and related assurance, risk management, control, and governance functions. Internal auditing is an independent and objective assurance and consulting activity that helps organizations evaluate and improve the effectiveness of their risk management, internal control, and governance processes. The program therefore goes beyond basic accounting and develops competencies in internal auditing, financial accounting and reporting, cost and management accounting, management accounting and control, taxation, accounting information systems, business management, and related areas.

courses.course_name: Bachelor of Arts in Islamic Studies major in Political Economy
courses.course_description: The Bachelor of Arts in Islamic Studies major in Political Economy is a humanities and social-science-oriented program that studies Islam as a way of life while examining its relationships with economic, social, cultural, political, and legal systems. The Political Economy specialization applies this Islamic Studies foundation to the relationship between political structures, economic conditions, governance, society, and development. Students study Islamic history, Qur'an and Hadith, Arabic, Islamic philosophy and culture, Sharia, politics, economics, and contemporary social issues. The program is intended to develop graduates who can analyze political and economic issues from perspectives informed by Islamic thought and who can work in multicultural, pluralistic, and community-oriented environments.

Analysis of political and economic events
Understanding of Islamic philosophy and culture

Understanding of Muslim communities and multicultural contexts

courses.course_name: Bachelor of Arts in Journalism
courses.course_description: The Bachelor of Arts in Journalism (BA Journalism) is a four-year undergraduate program that prepares students to gather, investigate, verify, analyze, write, edit, produce, and disseminate news and other journalistic content across print, broadcast, digital, and other media platforms. Journalism focuses on identifying and reporting newsworthy events, issues, and developments that are relevant to the communities served by journalists. The program combines journalistic research and writing with media production, editing, communication, social-science concepts, media law, and professional ethics. The program also emphasizes the role of journalism in a democratic society, requiring students to develop professional judgment, accuracy, ethical responsibility, and awareness of the social impact of news and information.

courses.course_name: Bachelor of Landscape Architecture
courses.course_description: The Bachelor of Landscape Architecture (BLA) is a professional undergraduate program focused on the study, planning, design, development, and management of outdoor environments for human use and enjoyment. The field combines design, environmental science, ecology, natural and social sciences, landscape technology, and engineering concepts to create functional, aesthetically appropriate, sustainable, and environmentally responsive outdoor spaces. Students learn to analyze sites and landscapes, develop design solutions, communicate designs graphically and verbally, and manage the implementation and evaluation of landscape projects. The program also emphasizes ecology, conservation, preservation, sustainable development, professional practice, legal and ethical responsibilities, and the relationship between people and their physical environment. Landscape architecture is also a regulated profession in the Philippines under Republic Act No. 9053, which defines its professional scope to include planning, designing, supervising, and administering the development of natural scenery and outdoor spaces, as well as environmental protection, conservation, and rehabilitation.
obtainable_skills: Basic engineering application to landscape projects
Knowledge of landscape-related laws and regulations

courses.course_name: Bachelor of Library and Information Science
courses.course_description: The Bachelor of Library and Information Science (BLIS) is a professional undergraduate program that prepares students to organize, manage, preserve, retrieve, evaluate, and provide access to information resources in libraries and other information environments. The program covers both traditional library services and modern information-management practices. Students learn how to identify and respond to users' information needs, organize and retrieve information resources, provide reference and information services, manage library resources, use library automation and information technologies, conduct research, and address legal and ethical issues involving information. The program therefore extends beyond traditional library work. It prepares graduates to work with information resources, digital systems, information users, library services, research, and information technologies.

courses.course_name: Bachelor of Science in Marine Transportation
courses.course_description: The Bachelor of Science in Marine Transportation (BSMT) is a higher education degree program that prepares students for careers as merchant marine deck officers. It covers competences defined under PQF level 6 and Table A-II/1 and some elements of Table A-II/2 of the STCW code, along with other national and international requirements. The program deals with the study of navigation, cargo handling and stowage, controlling the safe operation and care for persons on board the ship at the operational level. courses.course_name: Bachelor of Science in Mathematics
courses.course_description: The Bachelor of Science in Mathematics is an undergraduate program that provides students with a deep and broad understanding of mathematics as both a theoretical discipline and a practical tool. Mathematics is described as the science of patterns, where mathematicians seek to discover, analyze, and classify patterns in abstract objects and natural phenomena. The program covers traditional domains such as quantity (arithmetic), structure (algebra), space (geometry), and change (analysis). The program emphasizes distinctive mathematical modes of thought including abstraction, generalization, deduction, inference, use of symbols, and the axiomatic method.
obtainable_skills: Rigorous Argument and Proof: Construct and evaluate formal mathematical proofs and logical arguments.

Mechanical engineering is one of the broadest engineering disciplines, encompassing areas such as thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, solid mechanics, materials science, manufacturing, and energy systems.

courses.course_name: Bachelor of Science in Meteorology
courses.course_description: The Bachelor of Science in Meteorology is a four-year undergraduate program that provides students with a comprehensive and rigorous training in the study of weather processes and forecasting. Meteorology is a branch of atmospheric science that draws on basic knowledge, theory, and laws from physics, mathematics, and chemistry to develop a strong understanding of the physical and dynamical processes affecting atmospheric motions and behavior. The program covers the study of the atmosphere for various purposes, including severe and extreme weather systems (e.g., tropical cyclones), agriculture, military defense, navigation, and disaster risk reduction and management.

Disaster Risk Reduction: Apply meteorological knowledge to disaster risk reduction and management.

courses.course_description: The Bachelor of Science in Midwifery is a four-year undergraduate program that prepares students for careers as professional midwives. The program provides students with the theoretical knowledge and practical skills necessary to provide comprehensive maternal and newborn health care, including antenatal care, normal delivery, postpartum care, and family planning services. The curriculum integrates basic sciences, health sciences, and clinical midwifery training.
obtainable_skills: Antenatal Care: Provide comprehensive care to pregnant women, including assessment, monitoring, and health education.
Labor and Delivery Management: Manage normal labor and delivery, including emergency measures in case of complications.
Postpartum Care: Provide care to mothers during the postpartum period, including monitoring and health education.

courses.course_name: Bachelor of Science in Agricultural and Biosystems Engineering major in Land and Water Resources Engineering
courses.course_description: The Bachelor of Science in Agricultural and Biosystems Engineering (BSABE) is an engineering degree that applies engineering science and design to agricultural, biological, environmental, and natural-resource systems. The Land and Water Resources Engineering specialization focuses on the engineering planning, development, conservation, and management of land and water resources. Important applications include irrigation and drainage, soil and water conservation, land development, hydrology/agrometeorology, water-resource systems, dams, farm roads and bridges, and related agricultural and environmental infrastructure. The program combines engineering mathematics and sciences with agricultural and biological sciences, engineering design, resource management, and practical applications. Official university program descriptions identify land development, irrigation and drainage, soil and water resources, environmental management, and related infrastructure as major areas of BSABE practice. The specialization is also directly represented in the Philippine Agricultural and Biosystems Engineering profession. Republic Act No. 10915 identifies Land and Water Resources Engineering as one of the competency areas covered by the Agricultural and Biosystems Engineering licensure examination.
